title: Building Regulations
subtitle: Eight Building Regulations practice mocks
description: Eight Building Regulations practice mocks covering approved documents, Part P notification, dwelling scope, certification, ventilation, fire safety and practical compliance decisions.
format: Eight rotating 20-question practice mocks. Exam format: 40 minutes, open book. Pass at 60%+.

questions.prompt: Part 'A' of the building, states that horizontal chases should not be deeper than:
questions.explanation: Approved Document A limits chasing because cutting masonry removes load-bearing material. A horizontal chase severs a continuous band across the wall, weakening it more than a vertical one, so it is capped at one sixth of the wall thickness.

questions.prompt: A new build family house has just been completed, and it fully complies with the relevant building regulations. It has bedrooms and 2 reception rooms, how many low energy pendants are fitted?
questions.explanation: Approved Document L1 set minimum provision for low-energy fixed lighting in new dwellings. For the source example, the required proportion of low-energy pendants works out as three.

questions.prompt: Part 'M' of the building regulations, states the required height of a central heating roomstat would be:
questions.explanation: Approved Document M aims to make controls accessible to users. A room thermostat at about 1100 mm sits within the accessible control height band used by the source guidance.

questions.prompt: Part 'E' of the building regulations, does NOT cover:

options.A: An Internal wall which separates a bedroom from a family bathroom
options.B: An Internal wall which separates a room containing a WC from a hallway
options.C: An Internal wall which separates an en-suite bathroom from the associated bedroom
options.D: An internal wall which separates a integral garage from a kitchen

questions.explanation: Approved Document E deals with resistance to the passage of sound between rooms and dwellings. The source exception is the wall between an en-suite bathroom and its associated bedroom, which is not treated as a separate protected room boundary in the same way.

questions.prompt: Part 'A' of the building regulations, Does NOT cover:

options.C: The size of the floor joist

questions.explanation: Approved Document A is about structure, including foundations, floors, walls and roof structure. Window type is not a structural Part A item in the way the other options are.

questions.prompt: Part 'P' of the building regulations, Came into force on 1st January, in which year?
questions.explanation: Part P, electrical safety in dwellings, was introduced for domestic electrical work from 1 January 2005. That is why 2005 is the keyed date.

questions.prompt: How many alphabetical Parts are there to the building regulations?
questions.explanation: The Building Regulations group their technical requirements under letter-headed Parts, running A to P, which gives fourteen Parts. Each Part addresses a distinct subject such as structure, fire safety or electrical safety.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum permitted Ze measurement of a Domestic premises with a TN-S earthing system Installed:
questions.explanation: For a domestic TN-S supply, the commonly used maximum external earth fault loop impedance value is 0.8 ohm. That Ze value supports automatic disconnection under BS 7671.

questions.prompt: Which of the alphabetical parts of the building regulations would apply to the domestic electrical installer:
questions.explanation: Approved Document P is the Building Regulations guidance for electrical safety in dwellings. It is the Part most directly relevant to domestic electrical installers.

questions.prompt: The building regulations. States that ALL new and refurbished single family dwellings of not more than two habitable floors have:

options.A: A Smoke alarm no more than 2m from all bedroom doors
options.D: Smoke alarms permanently wired from a local lightning circuit

questions.explanation: Approved Document B covers fire safety and domestic fire detection. New and refurbished dwellings need mains-powered smoke alarms with standby battery backup, so battery backup is the essential feature here.

questions.prompt: A passive stack would come under which Part of the building regulations:
questions.explanation: Passive stack ventilation is a ventilation strategy, so it falls under Approved Document F. Part F deals with ventilation rates and methods for dwellings.

questions.prompt: How many parts to schedule two of the building regulations:
questions.explanation: Schedule 2 of the source-era Building Regulations grouped exempt buildings and work into seven Parts. The question is testing that structure rather than an electrical rule.

questions.prompt: Part 'A' of the building regulations, states that Vertical chases should not be deeper than:
questions.explanation: Approved Document A allows vertical chases to be deeper than horizontal ones because they run with the wall's vertical load path rather than cutting across it, but they are still capped at one third of the wall thickness to preserve strength.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would need be notified to the building control:

options.A: Installing new central heating control wiring
options.B: Installing wall lights to a lounge
options.C: Replacing a damaged socket outlet in a kitchen
options.D: Upgrading the main Equipotential bonding conductors

questions.explanation: Under the source-era Part P notification examples, installing new central-heating control wiring is fixed electrical installation work associated with a controlled service. The other options are treated as minor work in that mock context.

questions.prompt: Which of the following need NOT be notified to building control:

options.A: An Extension to the LV garden lighting

questions.explanation: Part P notification covers fixed electrical installations in a dwelling and listed generation such as PV and microCHP. A self-contained solar garden light has no mains connection and is not part of the fixed installation, so it is not notifiable.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a special location:
questions.explanation: Special locations are higher-risk places such as rooms with baths or showers, pools and hot-air saunas. A cloakroom without a bath or shower is not one of those special locations.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a special Installation:

options.B: Electric underfloor heating in a conservatory

questions.explanation: The source-era Approved Document P list of special installations included electric floor and ceiling heating systems. Electric underfloor heating in the conservatory therefore fits that category.

questions.prompt: Part 'M' of the building regulations does NOT apply to:
questions.explanation: Part M sets accessibility standards so everyday switches, sockets and communication controls are reachable and usable. A cooker switch is not among the accessories it covers, whereas socket outlets, telephone points and bell pushes are.

questions.prompt: When would you NOT need to inform building control after installing new 12V recessed lighting to a kitchen:

options.A: When the new lights are pre-assembled CE marked units
options.B: When the work was carried out in a disabled adapted house or flat
options.C: When they satisfy parts B & C of the building regulations
options.D: When you have installed suitable fireproof hoods to the lights

questions.explanation: The source-era Part P examples excluded pre-assembled CE-marked extra-low-voltage lighting sets from notification. If the 12 V recessed lights are such units, that is why Building Control need not be informed in this question.

questions.prompt: Which of the following rooms would require the largest ventilations fan:
questions.explanation: Approved Document F requires higher extract ventilation for kitchens because cooking produces moisture, heat and odours. A kitchen therefore needs the largest fan of the rooms listed.

questions.prompt: A 2.5mm² radial socket outlet circuit spans no more than 50 m² floor surface. The protective device fitted should be rated at?
questions.explanation: The On-Site Guide standard circuit arrangements allow a 2.5 mm2 radial socket circuit serving up to 50 m2 to be protected at 20 A. The rating protects the cable while allowing the expected socket load.

questions.prompt: For the purposes of equipotential bonding, earth clamps should be?

options.A: BS591 clamps with a warning label
options.B: BS591 clamps without a warning label
options.C: BS951 clamps with a warning label

questions.explanation: Main and supplementary bonding clamps should be BS 951 clamps and carry the safety warning label. The label helps prevent accidental removal of a bonding connection.

questions.prompt: The Requirements for Electrical Installations is published by the IET and is?

options.A: A British Standard code of practice
options.D: To be used by supervisors only

questions.explanation: BS 7671 is the IET Requirements for Electrical Installations and is a British Standard code of practice. It is not itself an Act or statutory instrument, although following it is the usual route to Part P compliance.

questions.prompt: When referring to special locations, the connection between extraneous conductors and CPC is known as?
questions.explanation: In special locations, supplementary bonding connects extraneous-conductive-parts to protective conductors where required. The aim is to reduce dangerous touch voltages in higher-risk surroundings.

questions.prompt: During initial verification, copies of certificates containing all necessary information can be found in?
questions.explanation: The IET On-Site Guide includes model certificates and schedules used for initial verification. That makes it the practical reference for the certificate information in this question.

questions.prompt: If a ring final socket outlet circuit is protected by a 32A MCB, it should be supplied with?
questions.explanation: A standard domestic ring final circuit protected by a 32 A device is normally wired in 2.5 mm2 twin-and-earth cable. The ring arrangement shares load around the two legs of the circuit.

questions.prompt: Who has the right to self-certify their work complies with Building Regulations?
questions.explanation: Competent Person Scheme members can self-certify that their domestic work complies with the Building Regulations. That route avoids a separate Building Control inspection for work they are registered to undertake.

questions.prompt: It is important to consider 'special locations' because?

options.A: Electrical installations are more common in these areas
options.B: There is a higher risk in these areas
options.C: There is always water in these areas
options.D: They are more accessible to the public

questions.explanation: Special locations need extra consideration because shock risk is increased by water, reduced body resistance, conductive surroundings or public use. The point is risk, not simply how common the installation is.

questions.prompt: A common installation method for lighting circuits is known as?
questions.explanation: The usual domestic lighting wiring method is the loop-in system, where permanent line, switched line and neutral connections are looped at ceiling roses or fittings. That is why "loop in" is the recognised term.

questions.prompt: Recommendations for standard final circuit arrangements for domestic power circuits can be found in?

options.A: BS 7671:2018 and the On Site Guide

questions.explanation: Standard final circuit arrangements for domestic power circuits are set out in BS 7671 and explained practically in the IET On-Site Guide. Those references give the circuit ratings, cable sizes and limits.

questions.prompt: What is the principle purpose of Part E of the Building Regulations?
questions.explanation: Approved Document E is the Building Regulations guidance for resistance to the passage of sound. Its purpose is sound insulation, not fire, thermal insulation or ventilation.

questions.prompt: The result of an earth fault loop impedance test will be expressed in?
questions.explanation: Earth fault loop impedance is an impedance measurement, so it is expressed in ohms. The result is used to check that protective devices will disconnect quickly enough.

questions.prompt: With the exception of SELV and PELV, the minimum value of insulation resistance is?
questions.explanation: For low-voltage circuits up to 500 V, a healthy insulation barrier must read at least 1.0 megohm; anything lower suggests deteriorated or damp insulation that could let current leak to earth. SELV and PELV are tested at a lower voltage with their own limits.

questions.prompt: What is the meaning of this symbol?

options.B: Light which can be covered by thermally insulating material
options.C: Light which can be installed into a flammable surface

questions.explanation: The symbol identifies a luminaire suitable for mounting on a normally flammable surface. It is therefore about where the light can be installed, not a heat or smoke detector symbol.

questions.prompt: Within a domestic situation, the correct disconnection time would be?
questions.explanation: For ordinary final circuits in domestic TN installations, BS 7671 automatic disconnection is commonly 0.4 seconds. That fast disconnection reduces the duration of electric shock under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: Which of these is not a responsibility of the Duty Holder in an Assessed Enterprise?

options.A: Ensuring that the results of the inspection and testing are accurately recorded on the appropriate forms of certification
options.B: Have an understanding of, and be responsible for the health and safety and other statutory requirements relating to electrical installation work in dwellings carried out by the enterprise
options.C: To ensure that the enterprise carries out all electrical installation work in dwellings in accordance with the relevant standards, including the issue of certification
options.D: To ensure that the enterprise carries out all electrical installation work in dwellings in compliance with all relevant statutory requirements, including the issue of certification

questions.explanation: The Duty Holder carries overall accountability for legal compliance, competence and standards across the enterprise. Accurately recording inspection and test results on the certification forms is the technical task of the person actually carrying out and certifying the work, not a defined Duty Holder responsibility.

questions.prompt: A consumer unit that has a missing blank plate would contravene?

options.B: Part P of the Building Regulations
options.C: Section 701 of the IET Wiring Regulations

questions.explanation: A missing consumer-unit blank exposes an opening that can fail the required enclosure IP protection against finger access to live parts. That is why the defect is an IP rating issue.

questions.prompt: For how many hours does emergency lighting need to operate in places of entertainment and for sleeping risk?
questions.explanation: Emergency lighting for places of entertainment and sleeping risk is commonly specified for a 3-hour duration. The longer duration supports safe evacuation and possible reoccupation decisions.

questions.prompt: You would perform an insulation resistance test in order to?

options.A: Ensure a circuit will disconnect within the required time
options.B: Prove the continuity of the protective conductor
options.C: Test the correct functioning of the mechanical parts of an RCD
options.D: Verify that there is no breakdown in the insulation of the conductor

questions.explanation: An insulation resistance test checks that conductors are properly insulated from each other and from earth. It is used to find insulation breakdown, not to prove disconnection time or RCD operation.

questions.prompt: Where three core twin and cpc cable is used for lighting circuits, the colour that should not be used as neutral is?
questions.explanation: In harmonised three-core-and-CPC cable, brown, black and grey are line conductor colours unless correctly identified otherwise. Black should not simply be used as neutral; neutral should be blue.

questions.prompt: In a two storey domestic house with three bedrooms, a kitchen with a door and a total floor area of less than 200m² per floor, what is the minimum number of smoke alarms required?
questions.explanation: Approved Document B expects smoke alarms on the escape route of each storey in a dwelling. A two-storey house therefore needs at least two alarms.

questions.prompt: Identify one of the following which would definitely have an area which is classed as a 'special location'?
questions.explanation: Under BS 7671 Part 7 the classic special location is a room containing a bath or shower (Section 701), so a bathroom always contains such a location. A kitchen is not a special location in BS 7671 — treating it as one is a hangover from pre-2013 Part P notification rules — and a bedroom or a garden is not a special location either.

questions.prompt: During initial verification, copies of certificates containing all necessary information can be found in?
questions.explanation: The IET On-Site Guide includes examples of certificates and schedules for initial verification. It is the everyday reference for the necessary certificate information.

questions.prompt: A switch installed for permanently connected equipment should be?

options.A: Identified according to the equipment supplied

questions.explanation: A switch for permanently connected equipment should clearly identify the equipment it controls. That prevents the wrong item being isolated or operated during use and maintenance.

questions.prompt: Strappers on a two way lighting circuit should be?

options.B: Marked with 2 grooves to indicate line conductors
options.C: Sleeved blue to indicate neutral conductors
options.D: Sleeved brown to indicate line conductors

questions.explanation: Two-way lighting strappers are live conductors, not neutrals. Sleeving them brown makes their line function clear under BS 7671 identification practice.

questions.prompt: One of the requirements for initial verification on a completed installation is that?

options.A: All parts of the installation are correctly selected and erected
options.B: The On Site Guide is referenced to ensure the correct Ze of the circuit
options.C: The completed installation is checked at least twice
options.D: The installation is checked by a supervisor

questions.explanation: Initial verification includes checking that equipment has been correctly selected and erected before the installation is energised or certified. This is a core BS 7671 verification requirement.

questions.prompt: When calculating the maximum current demand of a cooker circuit, you can refer to?
questions.explanation: The On-Site Guide gives practical diversity guidance for cooker circuits. It is the reference used to estimate maximum demand rather than simply adding the full appliance rating.

questions.prompt: The minimum distance a fixed data broadband cable should be installed away from 230v services is?
questions.explanation: Keeping data cabling at least 50 mm from 230 V mains limits electromagnetic interference that would corrupt the signal, and reduces the chance of insulation breakdown putting mains voltage onto the data system. Greater separation is only needed for higher-power runs.

questions.prompt: When supplying remote installations, SWA is often preferred as?

options.C: It is a cheaper method for long cable runs

questions.explanation: SWA cable has steel wire armour that gives strong mechanical protection. That makes it a common choice for remote supplies and buried or exposed runs.

questions.prompt: A 30mA RCD used for additional protection, provides protection against?
questions.explanation: A 30 mA RCD used for additional protection detects residual current leaking from line to earth. It is shock protection, not overload or short-circuit protection.

questions.prompt: The purpose of the Competent Persons Scheme is to?

options.A: Encourage electrical engineers to further their education
options.B: Ensure checks are carried out on persons involved in electrical installation work
options.C: Maintain a register of competent persons, allowing certification of work to pass to registered competent schemes as opposed to directly to building control
options.D: Provide reassurance to customers requesting electrical work

questions.explanation: The Competent Person Scheme provides a route for registered installers to certify domestic work through their scheme rather than applying directly to Building Control. That is the Part P self-certification route.

questions.prompt: A convenient and satisfactory method of fixing items to a plasterboard partition wall would be?
questions.explanation: Self-drilling spiral plugs are designed to grip plasterboard without needing a solid masonry backing. They are a convenient fixing method for light accessories on plasterboard partitions.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following regulations is not an approved document?

options.B: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002
options.C: Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations 1992
options.D: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998

questions.explanation: "BS7677 New Wiring Regulations 2011" is a made-up name: the wiring standard is BS 7671 (not BS 7677), and the 2011 change was Amendment 1 to BS 7671:2008 — today it is BS 7671:2018+A2:2022. BS 7671 is a non-statutory British Standard, whereas B, C and D (ESQCR, PPE at Work, PUWER) are genuine statutory regulations, so A is the odd one out. Strictly, "Approved Document" means Building Regulations guidance (Parts A to R), so the question really asks which item is the invented, non-statutory one — still A.

questions.prompt: Horizontal chases in walls should be no thicker than?
questions.explanation: Cutting too deep into a wall removes load-bearing material and weakens it, so structural guidance caps horizontal chases at one sixth of the wall thickness. This keeps enough sound masonry to carry loads safely above and around the chase.

questions.prompt: The EAWR states that any persons working on electrical installations should be?

options.A: Able to prove he/she has worked on an identical installation previously
options.D: Registered on a competent persons scheme

questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations require people working on electrical systems to be competent for the work they undertake. Competence is the legal test, not membership of a particular scheme by itself.

questions.prompt: What is the principle purpose of Part F of the Building Regulations?
questions.explanation: Approved Document F is the Building Regulations guidance for ventilation. It covers provision of fresh air and extract ventilation in buildings.

questions.prompt: Two core flexible cable to BS EN 50525 has the colours?
questions.explanation: Two-core flexible cable uses brown for line and blue for neutral under harmonised conductor colours. Those colours make polarity clear.

questions.prompt: When performing a safe isolation test and safely locking off the circuit, the key should be kept?

options.A: Close to the consumer unit in case of emergency
options.D: With the person who isolated the circuit

questions.explanation: The lock-off key should stay with the person who isolated the circuit. That prevents someone else re-energising the circuit while work is being carried out.

questions.prompt: Which part of the building regulations refers to the conservation of fuel and power?
questions.explanation: Part L is the Building Regulations Part for conservation of fuel and power. Electrical installers meet it most often through lighting and energy-efficiency requirements.

questions.prompt: A consumer unit that has a missing blank plate would contravene?

options.B: Part P of the Building Regulations
options.C: Section 701 of the IET Wiring Regulations

questions.explanation: A missing consumer-unit blank compromises the enclosure IP rating by leaving live parts more accessible. The immediate compliance issue is therefore ingress and finger-access protection.

questions.prompt: The selection and installation of lighting diffusers which form part of a ceiling are subject to certain requirements of:

options.D: Code of Practice for rafter roofs

questions.explanation: Approved Document B covers fire safety, including how ceiling linings and fittings behave in fire. Lighting diffusers forming part of a ceiling must not undermine that fire performance.

questions.prompt: Energy efficient systems come under the scrutiny of the Building Regulations:
questions.explanation: Energy-efficient systems fall under Part L, conservation of fuel and power. That Part drives efficient lighting, heating controls and energy performance provisions.

questions.prompt: The Building Regulations are divided into:
questions.explanation: The source-era Building Regulations were commonly taught as 14 alphabetical Parts. The question is testing that older Part count.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a term normally used to express the objectives or 'functional requirements' of the Building Regulations:
questions.explanation: Functional requirements in the Building Regulations use terms such as adequate, appropriate and reasonable. "Usual" is not the normal wording for a requirement.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not classed as 'Minor Work' under Part P of the Building Regulations:

options.A: Adding a 'spur' to a living room ring circuit
options.B: Replacing a broken 13A socket in a bedroom
options.C: Replacing damaged cable in a ground floor radial circuit

questions.explanation: Upgrading an electric shower adds significant load in a high-risk wet location, often needing a larger cable, new circuit and protective measures, so it is notifiable work requiring inspection. Replacing a socket or adding a spur are simple like-for-like jobs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not be classed as a 'special location':
questions.explanation: Special locations are higher-risk areas such as swimming pools, gardens and certain extra-low-voltage lighting where water or outdoor conditions increase shock danger. An ordinary entrance hall is a dry, normal-risk space, so it carries no special requirements.

questions.prompt: The person or organisation responsible for the authorization of the 'competent persons scheme' is:
questions.explanation: Competent Person Schemes are authorised under the Building Regulations framework by the Secretary of State. Scheme membership then allows registered installers to self-certify relevant work.

questions.prompt: Part P does not apply to:

options.D: Share Amenities in blocks of flats

questions.explanation: Approved Document P applies to fixed electrical installations in dwellings and associated areas, but lifts are outside its scope. Lift safety is controlled through other specialist requirements.

questions.prompt: In the Part P document 'Extra Low Voltage' a.c. is defined as:
questions.explanation: Extra-low voltage is defined as not exceeding 50 V a.c., the agreed upper limit considered to present a much lower shock risk than mains voltage. Above this band, the energy available to drive dangerous current through the body rises sharply.

questions.prompt: The Part P document took effect on:
questions.explanation: Approved Document P came into force on 1 January 2005, introducing legal control over domestic electrical installation work to reduce deaths and fires from poor wiring. From that date such work in dwellings had to be notified or self-certified.

questions.prompt: Part P of the Building Regulations applies to:
questions.explanation: The source-era Part P document applied in England and Wales. Later devolution and amendments changed the current position, so this answer follows the mock source period.

questions.prompt: The Part P document requires that all electrical installation work has been selected and installed in accordance with:
questions.explanation: Part P requires domestic electrical work to be designed and installed safely, and BS 7671 is the recognised technical standard for doing that. The other standards listed are not wiring-installation rules.

questions.prompt: In accordance with Part P which of the following Regulations/Publications does not apply to work on electrical installations:

options.D: The Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002

questions.explanation: RIDDOR is an accident and dangerous-occurrence reporting regime, not a design or installation standard for electrical work. BS 7671, EWR and ESQCR are the relevant electrical safety references in this context.

questions.prompt: All electrical work carried out professionally is subject to statutory requirements laid out in the:
questions.explanation: Professional electrical work is subject to the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989. BS 7671 supports compliance, but EAWR is the statutory duty for safe electrical systems at work.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not classified as a 'special location and installation' under Part P:
questions.explanation: The source-era Part P special-location and special-installation list includes items such as hot-air saunas, PV and small-scale generators. Industrial fluorescent lighting is not one of those Part P special categories.

questions.prompt: A firm seeking 'competent person' status has to have someone responsible for day-to-day quality and standards. This person is called the:
questions.explanation: A Competent Person Scheme requires a named individual who oversees daily technical quality and ensures work meets the standards; this role is the Qualified Supervisor. They are the firm's technical anchor for self-certification, distinct from general managers.

questions.prompt: The Building Act 1984 is policed by:
questions.explanation: Local authorities enforce the Building Act and Building Regulations in their areas. That is why they are the body described as policing the Building Act here.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are not exempt from the Building Regulations:

options.B: Buildings belonging to the Civil Aviation Authority
options.C: Buildings belonging to the United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority
options.D: Most buildings belonging to the Crown

questions.explanation: The source exemptions covered certain specialist bodies, but ordinary Crown buildings were not generally exempt in the way implied by the other options. The answer is therefore "most buildings belonging to the Crown".

questions.prompt: Approved document K sets out requirements applying to protection from falling, collision and:
questions.explanation: Approved Document K covers protection from falling, collision and impact. Impact is the missing hazard in that Part K title.

questions.prompt: Approved document N applies to glazing. Which of the following is not considered a safety issue within the document:
questions.explanation: Approved Document N addresses glazing hazards from people striking, opening or cleaning glass safely. Damp is a moisture and weatherproofing concern dealt with elsewhere, so it is not a glazing safety issue under this document.

questions.prompt: Approved document A requires notches in joist to be no greater than 0.125 times the:
questions.explanation: A notch removes timber from the top or bottom edge of a joist, where bending stresses are greatest, so it is limited to 0.125 (one eighth) of the joist depth. Keeping notches small relative to depth leaves enough sound timber to carry the floor load safely.

questions.prompt: When a British Standard has an equivalent European Standard which of the following statements apply:

options.B: Either Standard may be worked to
options.C: Only the British Standard shall be applied
options.D: Only the European Standard shall be applied

questions.explanation: When a British Standard is harmonised with its European equivalent it becomes a dual-numbered BS EN document, so both designations refer to the same requirements and are applied together as one standard rather than as competing alternatives.

questions.prompt: What does Approved Document M give guidance on:

options.C: Resistance to the passage of sound
options.D: Resistance to the spread of fire

questions.explanation: Approved Document M is about access to and use of buildings. It gives guidance on making buildings and controls usable by a wide range of occupants.

questions.prompt: Holes in joists should be apart by at least:
questions.explanation: Holes too close together create a continuous line of weakness that the joist can split or shear along. Spacing them at least three hole diameters apart leaves enough solid timber between holes to keep the joist strong in bending and shear.

questions.prompt: Which of the following organizations gives accreditation to certification schemes:
questions.explanation: UKAS, the United Kingdom Accreditation Service, is the national body that assesses and accredits the certification schemes and bodies themselves. The others are membership or awarding organisations operating schemes, not the accreditation authority that oversees them.

questions.prompt: Approved document B requires smoke alarms to be mounted on a ceiling at a distance from walls and light fittings of at least:
questions.explanation: Approved Document B fire guidance places smoke alarms away from walls and light fittings so smoke can reach them reliably and nuisance effects are reduced. The source distance is at least 300 mm.

questions.prompt: In the event of a current carrying cable being surrounded by insulating material for a length of 500mm or more both. Approved document E and BS 7671 require the current carrying capacity of the cable be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Thermal insulation around a current-carrying cable traps heat and reduces its current-carrying capacity. For 500 mm or more surrounded by insulation, the source BS 7671/Approved Document E guidance applies a 0.5 rating factor.

questions.prompt: Part L1 of the Building Regulations require reasonable provision be made for the conservation of power. One way of complying is to provide fixed lighting points that can only take lamps having a luminous efficacy greater than:
questions.explanation: The source-era Approved Document L1 lighting guidance used 40 lumens per circuit-watt as the high-efficacy threshold. Fixed lighting above that efficacy counted toward reasonable provision for energy conservation.

questions.prompt: Approved document M 'Access to and use of buildings' requires switches and sockets to be at 'appropriate heights'. The recommended minimum and maximum heights for fixing switches and sockets are:
questions.explanation: Approved Document M recommends accessible heights for switches and socket outlets. The familiar source range is 450 mm to 1200 mm above finished floor level.

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations was created in:
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations were made in 1989. They impose statutory duties for safe electrical systems and work practices.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT considered as a special location by BS7671 or Approved document P:

options.D: A room used for office work, likely to contain computers and electronic equipment

questions.explanation: A kitchen is a common Part P trap: it was treated specially in older domestic notification examples, but it is not a BS 7671 Part 7 special location like a bath/shower room or pool. That is why the source keys kitchen here.

questions.prompt: Which of the following commercial buildings electrical installations would approved document P apply to:

options.A: A public house with a flat over, fed from a common electricity supply
options.B: A public house with a flat over, fed from a separate electricity supply
options.C: A public house with private function rooms over it
options.D: A public house within a larger shopping complex

questions.explanation: Approved Document P can apply to mixed-use premises where the domestic accommodation and business share a common electrical supply. A public house with a flat over on the same supply fits that scope.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a requirement of a sole trader applying to become 'a competent person':

options.A: To carry out electrical installations work, submitting examples for assessment
options.B: To carry out the full range of electrical test as required by BS7671
options.C: To demonstrate at least 3 years electrical installation experience
options.D: To show evidence of issuing electrical installation certificates in accordance with BS7671

questions.explanation: Competent Person Scheme entry is based on assessment of work, testing ability and certification systems. A fixed requirement to prove at least three years of experience is not the source requirement.

questions.prompt: When might work on extra low voltage wiring and equipment for the purpose of control, need to be notified to building control.:

options.A: When work is carried out in a bedroom
options.B: When work is carried out in a kitchen
options.C: When work is carried out in a lounge
options.D: When work is carried out in a swimming pool

questions.explanation: Extra-low-voltage control wiring may still be notifiable when it is installed in a special location such as a swimming pool. Part P notification depends on both the type of work and where it is installed.

questions.prompt: Which field does approved document 'B' give guidance on:
questions.explanation: Approved Document B is the fire safety document, and fire detection and warning systems sit within that subject. Energy, fresh air and sound belong to Parts L, F and E respectively.

questions.prompt: You have to install a ventilation fan in a room, when would it be essential to check the ventilation rates and take appropriate measures:

options.A: When the fan is in a room with a combustion appliance with a balanced flue (sealed room)
options.B: When the fan is in a room with a combustion appliance with an open flue
options.C: When the fan is in a room with no combustion appliances but has many opening windows
options.D: When the fan is in a room with no combustion appliances, but has opening windows

questions.explanation: Whenever an extract fan shares a room with any combustion appliance, the fan can lower room pressure and disturb the air the appliance needs, so ventilation rates must be verified before installing it to avoid drawing combustion products, including carbon monoxide, back into the room. The presence of a combustion appliance, balanced flue or otherwise, is the trigger for that check.

questions.prompt: Approved document 'L' covers:

options.A: Conservation of fuel and power in dwellings
options.B: Conservation of power and light in dwellings
options.C: Preservation of fuel and power dwellings
options.D: Preservation of power and light in dwellings

questions.explanation: Approved Document L covers conservation of fuel and power. L1 is the domestic-dwelling side of that energy-efficiency guidance.

questions.prompt: Which of the following work is classed as a special installation according to approved document 'P':
questions.explanation: The source-era Approved Document P list of special installations included electric floor and ceiling heating systems. A 230 V electric underfloor heating installation therefore fits that special-installation category.

questions.prompt: With regards to management systems covering workmanship, regulation 7 of the building regulations indicates that quality standards are detailed in which publication:
questions.explanation: Regulation 7 covers materials and workmanship, and a recognised way to demonstrate consistent quality control is an accredited management system. BS EN ISO 9000 is the family of quality-management standards referenced for this purpose, unlike the fire, emergency-lighting and wiring standards listed.

questions.prompt: Certain electrical installation work is defined as 'Building Work' under the building regulations as it:

options.B: Involves work which builders typically undertake
options.C: Many constitute a service or fittings which is a controlled service under the building regulation
options.D: Will involve services, which all habitable room require

questions.explanation: Electrical installation work can be Building Work because it may install or alter a controlled service or fitting. Part P is the Building Regulations route for that controlled electrical service in dwellings.

questions.prompt: Approved document are different from building regulations as they do NOT contain:
questions.explanation: Approved Documents give guidance, examples and acceptable approaches, but they are not a catalogue of mandatory solutions for every design. Other approaches can comply if they meet the underlying Building Regulations requirements.

questions.prompt: Under the building regulations which of the following projects would NOT be under control of the building surveyor:

options.B: A conversion of a large house into flats
options.D: A loft conversion to 2 habitable rooms

questions.explanation: A small open-sided car port is generally exempt because it is a low-risk, open structure not used as habitable space. Converting a house into flats, extending a kitchen or creating loft rooms all alter habitable accommodation and structure, so they need Building Control approval.

questions.prompt: Which of the following electrical installation activates would NOT require notification to building control, when carried out by a person who is NOT registered with a competent person scheme:

options.A: Altering an existing circuit that supplies socket outlets to enable to be taken to a spa bath pump
options.B: Amending an existing circuit supplying socket outlets in the kitchen
options.C: Installation of a new dedicated supply circuit for a audio system in the lounge
options.D: Installation of main Equipotential bonging conductors and/or supplementary bonding conductors

questions.explanation: Main or supplementary bonding work alone is treated as non-notifiable in this source Part P context. The other options involve work in higher-risk or new-circuit situations that trigger notification.

questions.prompt: According to the building regulations 2000, which regulation is entitled 'The meaning of Building work':
questions.explanation: In the Building Regulations 2000, Regulation 3 sets out what counts as 'building work', such as erection, extension and material alterations. This definition determines whether the Regulations apply to a given job at all.

questions.prompt: Where would you find details of notification procedures to follow when starting, carrying out and completing building work:

options.C: The construction, Design and management regulations 1994
options.D: The health and safety at work act 1974

questions.explanation: The procedural rules for giving notices, starting work and completion sit in Part V of the Building Regulations 2000 source framework. Approved Document P gives technical guidance, not the full procedural machinery.

questions.prompt: When an equivalent new European standard is published, what normally happens to the British standard:

options.A: Both British standard and the European standard will apply and both must be complied with simultaneously
options.B: Either standard can be adopted for a project and the contractor may choose which standard to comply with
options.C: The British standard is either immediately withdrawn or withdrawn on a defined basis
options.D: The British standard remains in place and will always take precedence in the UK over other documents

questions.explanation: When a European standard supersedes a British Standard, the old British Standard is normally withdrawn immediately or by a stated withdrawal date. That avoids two conflicting national standards remaining in force indefinitely.

questions.prompt: Approved document F requirement F1 does NOT apply to:

options.A: A garage used in connection with a single dwelling
options.B: A small kitchen inn a flat above ground level
options.D: Utility rooms that are located more than 50m away from the kitchen

questions.explanation: Ventilation requirements target habitable and moisture-producing rooms where people spend time or where pollutants and water vapour build up. A garage attached to a single dwelling is not an occupied living space of that kind, so the requirement does not apply to it, whereas kitchens, bathrooms and utility rooms all need controlled ventilation.

questions.prompt: Regulations 7 of the building regulations require that building work is carried out

options.B: In the most cost effective manner

questions.explanation: Regulation 7 requires building work to be carried out in a workmanlike manner. It is about proper workmanship, not speed or cost.

questions.prompt: An electrical cable route penetrates the ceiling/floor between two flats, there are specific issues that need to be addressed with regards to minimising the passage of sound between the two flats. Which document would you refer to for guidance:
questions.explanation: Approved Document E deals with resistance to the passage of sound. A service penetration between flats needs acoustic sealing and detailing, so Part E is the relevant guidance.

questions.prompt: What does Approved document L1 NOT give guidance on:

options.A: Conservation of fuel and power in non domestic buildings

questions.explanation: Approved Document L1 is the dwelling guidance for conservation of fuel and power. Non-domestic energy conservation is covered separately, so it is not within L1.

questions.prompt: Approved document M gives guidance on accessibility of switches and sockets in dwellings and other buildings, in which parts of the building does this guidance apply:

options.B: In rooms only on ground level
options.C: Only in rooms designed by the building owner
options.D: Only in the rooms of a domestic dwelling where a wheelchair bound person lives

questions.explanation: Approved Document M guidance on accessible switches and sockets is intended for habitable rooms generally, not only wheelchair-adapted homes or ground-floor rooms. That is why "all habitable rooms" is the best fit.

questions.prompt: In practice, for a business or individual to become a member of one of the competent person schemes, they must:

options.A: Confirm in writing to the scheme provider the level of technical competence of the operative whom is responsible for carrying out the electrical installation work
options.B: Register with the local building control service and pay a annual subscription fee
options.C: Register with the local building control service and pay them notification/inspection fee for every notifiable undertaken
options.D: Undertake electrical work in dwellings, undergo in initial technical assessment and thereafter undergo periodic surveillance by the competent person scheme

questions.explanation: Competent Person Scheme membership requires technical assessment and ongoing surveillance by the scheme provider. It is not simply a subscription or a one-off declaration to Building Control.

questions.prompt: The building regulations are made under powers in the building act 1984 and apply in England and Wales. The current edition of the building regulations are:
questions.explanation: The mock is using the older source context in which the Building Regulations 2000 were the current edition. In current England practice the 2010 Regulations have replaced that, but the preserved answer follows the source.

questions.prompt: Regulation 7 (Materials & Workmanship) of the building regulations requires that building work is to be carried out:

options.A: Only after all the relevant paperwork has been completed
options.D: With all the correct tools for the job

questions.explanation: Regulation 7 requires proper materials as well as proper workmanship. "Adequate and proper materials" is the substance of that duty.

questions.prompt: A new greenhouse is being constructed, when would the electrical installation within it need to comply with the requirements of Approved document P:

options.A: When the greenhouse forms part of a commercial farm complex
options.B: When the greenhouse is part if a retail garden centre that IS accessible to the public
options.C: When the greenhouse is part of retail garden centre that is NOT accessible to the public
options.D: When the greenhouse is within the grounds of a private dwelling

questions.explanation: Part P applies to electrical installations in dwellings and associated land or outbuildings. A greenhouse within the grounds of a private dwelling falls inside that domestic scope.

questions.prompt: The selection and installation of lighting diffusers which form part of a ceiling are subject to certain requirements of:

options.D: Code of Practice for rafter roofs

questions.explanation: Lighting diffusers that form part of a ceiling affect fire performance and surface spread of flame. That is why the relevant Building Regulations guidance is Approved Document B.

questions.prompt: Approved document A requires notches in joist to be no greater than 0.125 times the:
questions.explanation: Approved Document A limits notches in joists by reference to joist depth. The source limit is 0.125 times the depth, which is one eighth.

questions.prompt: In a two storey domestic house with three bedrooms, a kitchen with a door and a total floor area of less than 200m² per floor, what is the minimum number of smoke alarms required?
questions.explanation: Fire and smoke can spread between floors before occupants are aware of it, so detection is required on every storey containing accommodation. A two-storey house therefore needs at least one alarm per floor, giving a minimum of two interlinked smoke alarms.

questions.prompt: A 2.5mm² radial socket outlet circuit spans no more than 50 m² floor surface. The protective device fitted should be rated at?
questions.explanation: A 2.5 mm2 radial socket circuit serving no more than 50 m2 is a standard 20 A arrangement in the On-Site Guide. A 32 A device would be for a different circuit arrangement.

questions.prompt: Part 'A' of the building, states that horizontal chases should not be deeper than:
questions.explanation: Cutting a chase removes material and weakens the wall. Structural guidance limits horizontal chases to one sixth of the wall thickness so the remaining masonry keeps enough strength to carry its loads safely.

questions.prompt: Prior to the formal appointment of an Approved Inspector, what document needs to be provided to the local authority?
questions.explanation: An Approved Inspector route starts with an Initial Notice to the local authority. It tells the authority that the approved inspector will control the building work instead of local authority building control.

questions.prompt: When carrying out an insulation resistance test on a lighting circuit, you should ensure?

options.A: A connection is made between both switches
options.B: None of the switches are switched to the off position
options.C: None of the switches are switched to the on position
options.D: Two way switches are operated during the test

questions.explanation: On a lighting circuit with two-way switching, operating the switches during insulation resistance testing helps include all switched conductors and strapper paths. Otherwise part of the wiring could be missed.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum luminous rating of an energy efficient fixed light fitting?
questions.explanation: The source-era Approved Document L lighting threshold for an energy-efficient fixed light fitting is 40 lumens per circuit-watt. That figure was used to identify high-efficacy lighting.

questions.prompt: In a domestic TN system, the main earthing conductor size should be?
questions.explanation: For a typical domestic TN supply with common service conductor sizes, the main earthing conductor is commonly 16 mm2. The sizing supports safe fault-current return under BS 7671.

questions.prompt: Where incoming mains services are incorrectly bonded, the result can be?

options.A: An increased risk of electric shock
options.C: An increased risk of gas or water leaks

questions.explanation: Bonding keeps incoming metallic services and the electrical protective system at substantially the same potential. If bonding is wrong, dangerous touch voltages can remain and shock risk increases.

questions.prompt: An alternative method of testing the resistance of an earth electrode is by the use of?
questions.explanation: An earth loop impedance tester can be used as an alternative method to assess an earth electrode in suitable circumstances. It checks the earth path impedance rather than low-resistance continuity.

questions.prompt: What is the meaning of this symbol?

options.A: Downlight which must be operated within a protective shield
options.B: Light which can be covered by thermally insulating material
options.C: Light which can be installed into a flammable surface

questions.explanation: The symbol indicates a downlight or lamp arrangement that must be used with its protective shield. The shield is part of the safety design, so operating without it is not acceptable.

questions.prompt: Which compliance certificate is not required to be provided to a householder on completion of notifiable work?

options.C: Final certificate issued by an approved inspector

questions.explanation: Part P notifiable electrical work needs the appropriate electrical certificate and a Building Regulations completion or final certificate route. Planning approval is a separate planning-control matter, not a completion certificate for the electrical work.

questions.prompt: The building regulation part that refers to accessibility is?
questions.explanation: Part M is the Building Regulations Part for access to and use of buildings. It includes accessibility guidance for controls, switches and sockets.

questions.prompt: A lighting circuit installed in a domestic property would usually have a protective device rated at?
questions.explanation: Domestic lighting circuits are commonly protected by a 6 A device. That rating suits typical lighting loads and protects the usual lighting-circuit cable size.

questions.prompt: For how many hours does emergency lighting need to operate in places of entertainment and for sleeping risk?
questions.explanation: For places of entertainment and sleeping risk, emergency lighting is commonly specified with a 3-hour duration. That supports safe evacuation and resilience if the normal supply fails.

questions.prompt: Which of these ventilation systems is most common in new dwellings?

options.C: Continuous mechanical supply with heat recovery

questions.explanation: Background ventilators, such as trickle vents built into windows, are the simplest and cheapest way to provide continuous fresh-air change, so they are the most widely fitted provision in new homes compared with the more specialised mechanical systems.

questions.prompt: The number of socket outlets that can be installed on a standard BS1363 ring final circuit is?

options.C: Limited by the protective device rating

questions.explanation: BS 7671 does not set a fixed numerical limit on sockets on a standard ring final circuit. In practice the design is limited by load, floor area and protective device rating rather than by a set count.

questions.prompt: The Requirements for Electrical Installations is published by the IET and is?

options.A: A British Standard code of practice
options.D: To be used by supervisors only

questions.explanation: The IET Requirements for Electrical Installations, BS 7671, is a British Standard code of practice. It is widely used to demonstrate electrical safety, but it is not itself a statutory document.

questions.prompt: When replacing a 7kW shower unit with a new 10kW unit it, you must ensure?

options.A: The cable cpc will not fail under fault current
options.B: The cable size is adequate for the increased load
options.C: The new unit will provide sufficient flow
options.D: The unit will heat the water sufficiently

questions.explanation: A 10 kW shower draws more current than a 7 kW unit. Before replacement, the installer must confirm that the circuit cable and protective device are adequate for the increased load.

questions.prompt: A consumer unit that has a missing blank plate would contravene?

options.B: Part P of the Building Regulations
options.C: Section 701 of the IET Wiring Regulations

questions.explanation: A missing consumer-unit blank leaves the enclosure below its required IP protection against access to live parts. That makes the defect an IP rating issue.

questions.prompt: A member of a Competent Persons Scheme must?

options.A: Be of a sufficient competency to self-certify that their work has been carried out in compliance with the building regulations
options.B: Have all relevant and up to date qualifications
options.C: Have been a qualified electrician for at least 5 years
options.D: Have completed a relevant and recognised apprenticeship

questions.explanation: A Competent Person Scheme member must be competent enough to certify that their work complies with the Building Regulations. The scheme route is about assessed competence and self-certification, not a fixed apprenticeship history.

questions.prompt: When rewiring a socket outlet circuit in a domestic dwelling, the sockets outlets should be left at a height?

options.C: That is at least as high as their original position
options.D: That is easily reached without bending

questions.explanation: When rewiring an existing dwelling, accessibility should not be made worse. If sockets are not being repositioned to the new-build Part M height, they should at least be left no lower than their original position.

questions.prompt: An electrical contractor undertaking notifiable work can self-certify their work if?

options.A: Are on the competent persons register
options.B: Have been an electrical contractor for more than 5 years
options.C: Have been given permission by the local authority building control

questions.explanation: A contractor can self-certify notifiable domestic work only through registration with a Competent Person Scheme. Experience or apprenticeship alone does not provide the Building Regulations self-certification route.

questions.prompt: The year that The Construction, Design and Management Regulations first came into force was?
questions.explanation: The Construction (Design and Management) Regulations first came into force in 1995. They introduced construction health-and-safety duties for clients, designers and contractors.

questions.prompt: The maximum depth of a notch in a wooden joist should be

options.C: A maximum of 0.125 x joint depth

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, A maximum of 0.125 x joint depth is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which of these is not a requirement of Regulation 7 of the Building Regulations?

options.A: Building work shall be carried out in a workmanlike manner
options.B: Building work shall be carried out by registered competent persons only
options.C: Materials used in building work are applied, used or fixed so as to adequately perform the functions for which they are designed.
options.D: Building work shall be carried out with adequate and proper materials

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Building work shall be carried out by registered competent persons only is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Approved Document Part E (Resistance to the passage of sound) requires

options.A: Deep boxes to be used in separating walls
options.B: Sockets to be fitted back to back on a separating wall between a room and a corridor
options.C: Sockets to be staggered on opposite sides of a separating wall
options.D: That chases must be used in separating walls

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Sockets to be staggered on opposite sides of a separating wall is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which of these is non-notifiable work under Part P?

options.A: Work to connect an electric gate to an existing isolator
options.C: Installing an extractor fan 300mm from the edge of a bath at a height of 2m.
options.D: Installing a new outdoor lighting circuit in a garden

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Work to connect an electric gate to an existing isolator is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Approved documents L1A and L1B do not give guidance on the installation of
questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Solar photovoltaic panels is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum conductor cross sectional area for a radial circuit in a household protected by a 32A overcurrent device?
questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, 4.0mm Squared is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which of these cable installation methods has the highest maximum current carrying capacity (Iz)?
questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, C is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: An EV charging point can be connected to a PME supply, as long as one of the four provisions of Regulation: 722.411.4.1 are met, or, what else?

options.B: A tethered lead EV chargepoint is installed
options.C: 25mm squared bonding conductor is connected to all extraneous conductive parts
options.D: A Type F RCD is installed

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, An isolation transformer is used is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: It is necessary to notify the relevant building control body before the work begins if the work is

options.A: Carried out by an enterprise not registered with a CPS
options.B: Certified by a registered third party certifier
options.D: Carried out and certified by a registered competent enterprise

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Carried out by an enterprise not registered with a CPS is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum intermittent extract fan ventilation rate in a kitchen adjacent to a hob?
questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, 30 litres/ second is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which approved document requires sufficient means for giving early warning of fire?
questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, B is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: The statement is a requirement of which Approved Document? The building shall be designed and constructed so that there are appropriate provisions for the early warning of fire?
questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Approved Document Part B is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which of these is notifiable under Part P?

options.A: Electrical installation work in a shed that does not involve new outdoor wiring
options.B: The installation of a kitchen lighting system using a CE marked prefabricated, modular system linked by plug and socket connectors
options.C: New outdoor lighting circuit that involves crossing the garden
options.D: Electrical maintenance on equipment 700mm from Zone 1 in a bathroom

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, New outdoor lighting circuit that involves crossing the garden is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: A way of satisfying the requirements of approved document M is to install switches at a height

options.D: Between 450mm and 1200mm from the finished floor level

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Between 450mm and 1200mm from the finished floor level is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum spacing for gas installation pipework from an electricity meter?
questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, 150mm is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Vertical chases must

options.B: Be at least 50mm from the top or bottom of a joist
options.C: Not be deeper than one sixth of the wall thickness
options.D: Not be deeper than one third of the wall thickness

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Not be deeper than one third of the wall thickness is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Heat detectors should be mounted
questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Between 25mm to 150mm below the ceiling is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Part P does not apply to electrical installations

options.A: Outside a dwelling such as a pond pump in a garden
options.B: In outbuildings such as a detached garage
options.C: In business premises in the same building as a dwelling with separate metering
options.D: In the common access areas of blocks of flats such as corridors

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, In business premises in the same building as a dwelling with separate metering is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: In order to comply with the requirements of Approved Document Part C, persons carrying out electrical work in new buildings should

options.A: Seal cable entries to prevent the ingress of gas or water
options.B: Install switches at a height of between 450mm and 1200mm from the finished floor level
options.C: Provide fixed building services which are energy efficient
options.D: Fit background ventilators with intermittent extract fans

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Seal cable entries to prevent the ingress of gas or water is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Electrical testing should be carried out in the correct sequence. Which of the following is classed as the first live test?

options.A: Continuity of ring final circuit conductors

questions.explanation: Under the relevant Building Regulations and Approved Document guidance, Supply polarity is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

scoring.label: Strong — ready for Part P mock exam conditions
Pass — review missed source questions before moving on
Near miss — revise Part P scope and Approved Documents
Major gaps — rebuild Building Regulations fundamentals first

priorities: Notifiable work, special locations and the post-2013 Part P categories.
Approved Documents that affect electrical work: A, B, C, E, F, L, M, P and related duties.
Compliance routes through CPS notification, Building Control and correct certification.
Domestic scope: dwellings, gardens, outbuildings and common parts of residential buildings.
Read the wording carefully; the source tests use close distractors and regulatory exceptions.
